# Incident Report: Malware Infection on DESKTOP-H8ALZBV (10.8.15.133)

## Victim Host

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.8.15.133 |
| MAC | 00:1c:bf:03:54:82 (bound to this IP in ARP and as Ethernet source on all frames from it) |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-H8ALZBV (NBNS `<00>`/`<20>` registrations, mDNS, LLMNR, Kerberos CNameString `desktop-h8alzbv$`) |
| AD domain | LAFONTAINEBLEU.ORG (workgroup/NetBIOS name LAFONTAINEBLEU) |
| Logged-in user | **plucero** (Kerberos AS-REQ `CNameString: plucero`, realm LAFONTAINEBLEU, from 10.8.15.133) |
| Domain controller | 10.8.15.4 / WIN-JEGJIX7Q9RS.lafontainebleu.org (also 10.8.15.4 DHCP/DNS server) |

## Malware Family

**Attribution confidence: behavioral (no IDS/Suricata alert export was present in the evidence set, so this is not signature-confirmed).**

The behavior chain observed is a fake-invoice phishing lure delivering a padded JScript loader, which in turn uses Windows BITS to fetch a Win32 DLL payload and then establishes persistent HTTP C2 beaconing. This chain (brand-impersonation lure domain → oversized junk-padded `.js` inside a `.zip` → BITS-transferred DLL from the same IP → root-path `/` beacon with a legacy spoofed User-Agent) most closely matches the loader/downloader pattern documented for the **Latrodectus loader family**. I am naming it as the closest behavioral match, not a confirmed signature hit — treat the family label as provisional.

### Evidence for the chain
1. **Lure/delivery (t≈74.7s):** `10.8.15.133` GETs `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?...` (resolves to Cloudflare-fronted `104.21.55.70`). Response (frame 8659, HTTP 200, `application/octet-stream`) is a ZIP (`PK` magic bytes) containing `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js`.
2. **Padded loader:** the extracted `.js` is **6.99 MB**, almost entirely junk text (scraped PDF/technical-report content used as filler) — a known technique to inflate file size past AV/sandbox limits and hide a small malicious payload inside benign-looking noise.
3. **Second stage (t≈135.9-136.2s):** `10.8.15.133` uses **Microsoft BITS/7.8** (`User-Agent: Microsoft BITS/7.8`) to HEAD then GET `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` from a bare IP over port 80. The downloaded object is a **PE32+ DLL (x86-64)**.
4. **C2 beaconing (t≈197s through t≈1962s, i.e. ~29 minutes, 306 requests):** repeated GET/POST to `http://72.5.43.29/` (root path, no meaningful URI), all using a spoofed legacy User-Agent `Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)`. Several POSTs carry large encrypted/binary bodies (one up to 305 KB), consistent with a live command channel and possible data exfiltration, not passive telemetry.

## Indicators of Compromise
